newsitem.title: USA: Norand Corp soars on Western Atlas deal.
newsitem.headline: Norand Corp soars on Western Atlas deal.

text.p: Shares of Norand Corp soared about 40 percent Wednesday after the company said it agreed to be acquired by Western Atlas Inc.
Norand, which designs and develops mobile computing systems and wireless data communication networks, gained 13-1/2 to 32-7/8 in early morning trading.
"This is a great deal for Norand stockholders," said Richard Davis, an independent analyst with Richard W. Davis & Co.
"Norand had been in trouble about two years ago and has really done a good job of repairing things. Things have improved for them," Davis said.
Norand previously had accounting problems regarding sales in its European subsidiary, analysts said.
"This is a good deal for both parties," said John Grangaard, an analyst with GS2 Securities.
Under terms of the acquisition deal, Western Atlas will offer $33.50 a share for all 7.8 million shares of Norand common stock through a cash tender offer.

When completed, the deal will further strengthen the position of Western Atlas' Seattle-based Intermec division in the automated data collection (ADC) and mobile computing solutions industries, the companies said in a prepared statement.

"The merger of our company with Intermec combines two leaders in the global ADC industry that have complementary product and service lines, and this provides the base for excellent long-term growth," said Norand's Chairman N. Robert Hammer.
Western Atlas lost 1/2 to 71-5/8 in early morning trading.
